_doc: Mapping from intent (reads/runs/write/dispatches) → concrete action / command words. Users can edit this file to adjust boundaries. rules_dsl.py loads it to generate rules; on missing/broken file it falls back to built-in defaults.
_read_actions_doc: Semantic actions counted as 'read' after normalization (the action taken when an agent uses the read tool).
_read_shell_verbs_doc: Command words in shell counted as 'read file content' (when agent reads via shell, run_command starts with or contains these).
_read_idioms_doc: Finer regexes for idioms that are certainly reads (for Python etc.): json.load(, .read(), open(single-arg = read mode). If the command contains both these idioms and the target file, it counts as a read. Note: open('x','w') (comma present = write mode) will not match, so writes are not misclassified as reads.
_run_prefixes_doc: Regexes for 'prefix words' stripped from the head of subcommands during runs matching (they are not the actually invoked program): timeout N, sudo, env, KEY=val, nice, exec, python -m, etc. After stripping, check whether the head is the target command.
_write_shell_ops_doc: Shell write redirection operators / commands: >, >>, tee, dd. never_writes will consider a write when these are followed by the target.
_write_idioms_doc: Idioms that are certainly writes (Python etc.): open(...,'w'/'a'), .write(), json.dump(, .to_csv/.to_json. Writes inside scripts (path not in the command line) still cannot be captured.
